concept: Two rival requests, one rulebook, so the hero is built as a split: Mercedes' ask sits in muted grey and Williams' ask lands in white, setting up the twist that the richest and one of the smallest teams both want more money for opposite reasons. Slide 2 blows up the one number everything hangs on, $215m, and explains why it pinches now (factory spending moved inside it). Slides 3 and 4 mirror each other, one ask per slide, using the teams' own words, and slide 5 turns to the vote count and asks fans to pick a side. F1 red, type only: no driver photos, no team or F1 logos.
caption:
Mercedes wants more money. So does Williams.

F1's 2026 budget cap is $215m, but it now has to cover factory spending too, like wind tunnels, which used to have a separate limit.

Toto Wolff says Mercedes pitched the FIA an allowance to pay junior staff better, "not for more front wing", and admits it "didn't score a lot of brownie points".

Williams boss James Vowles wants something different: a catch-up where teams lower down the table get a bigger budget, the same way they already get extra wind tunnel time. Aston Martin's Adrian Newey says that logic fits. A 2027 change needs 6 of the 11 teams; The Race reported Audi, Aston Martin, Alpine and Cadillac in favour.

Should F1 help its smaller teams catch up, or keep one cap for all? Tell us below.
